items.outOfScope: Backend or database changes, the full-platform cutover, real identity data, third-party video hosting, autoplay, narration or production-readiness claims.
acceptance: The exact question and primary vote action are clear in the first viewport, with the existing demand poll immediately after the hero
The three-answer confirmation, final receipt, server-authoritative counts and reload persistence remain unchanged
One accessible self-hosted silent video shows synthetic question creation, voting and a published result
Concise visible copy retains voluntary self-selection, no identity or citizenship verification, another-browser repeatability and non-representativeness
Desktop, keyboard, 390x844, exact-head CI and hosted HTTPS checks pass without submitting a production response
items.verification: Run the focused demand test, types, both web builds, lint/public scan, media metadata and packaging checks, then verify local and hosted behavior in the retained in-app Browser.
items.privacy: Only synthetic local UI is captured. No identity selection, credential, key, production respondent, browser storage, console, local path or third-party media appears in the asset.
items.fixtures: Existing synthetic create form, open-poll choice and published 1/1/1 result from the local full-platform UI.
items.howToVerify: Follow issue #59 and docs/DEMAND_DEPLOYMENT.md; keep local, CI and hosted evidence distinct.

items.title: Adopt OpenVote brand and persistent poll action
items.goal: Give the public launch one recognizable brand and one continuously available path to the demand poll.
items.scope: Shared OpenVote mark and wordmark, one sticky demand CTA, direct poll anchor, concise nontechnical poll states and a re-captured synthetic walkthrough
items.outOfScope: Demand API, database, cookie behavior, confirmation/finality contract, full-platform voting behavior, Blueprint or Render-resource changes.
acceptance: Demand and full synthetic interfaces use the exact OpenVote name and one reusable accessible vector mark without the retired display name or badge
The demand landing has exactly one persistent Проголосувати CTA and its #poll target is not obscured by the sticky header
Normal and recorded demand states contain no browser/storage service messages while retaining a concise no-identity, no-citizenship, no-uniqueness and non-representativeness notice
The three answers, explicit confirmation, immutable server response, authoritative result sum and reload persistence remain unchanged
The updated silent walkthrough contains only established synthetic create, selected-choice and Published 1/1/1 states under the OpenVote brand
Desktop, keyboard, 390x844, exact-head CI and hosted HTTPS checks pass without submitting a production response
items.verification: Run focused demand tests, types, both web builds, lint/public scan, media metadata and Docker packaging; verify local and hosted behavior in the retained in-app Browser.
items.privacy: Only established synthetic local UI is captured. No identity selection, credential, key, production respondent, browser-storage message, console, local path or third-party media appears in the asset.
items.fixtures: Existing synthetic create form, open-poll choice without submission and Published 1/1/1 result.
items.howToVerify: Follow issue #62 and docs/DEMAND_DEPLOYMENT.md; keep local, CI and hosted evidence distinct.

items.title: Upgrade artifact upload action to Node 24
items.goal: Keep required public CI evidence uploads on a supported action runtime without changing their contracts.
items.scope: Replace both immutable actions/upload-artifact v4.6.2 pins with the reviewed official v7.0.2 commit.
items.outOfScope: Application, database, artifact contents, permissions, infrastructure, Render deployment or Browser behavior.
acceptance: Both upload steps use official actions/upload-artifact v7.0.2 commit cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9
Artifact names, paths and 14-day retention remain unchanged
Exact-head and merge-commit CI upload both artifacts without the deprecated Node.js 20 action annotation
items.verification: Run the bounded public scan and diff check, then require successful exact-head and merge workflows and inspect their annotations and uploaded artifact names.
items.privacy: Only existing bounded public evidence directories are uploaded; no private runtime material or credentials are added.
items.fixtures: Existing artifacts/reference and artifacts/release-ci outputs generated by the required workflow.

items.title: Enable repository vulnerability and CodeQL analysis
items.goal: Establish an explicit repository security-analysis baseline without changing application or deployment behavior.
items.scope: Enable vulnerability alerts, automated Dependabot security updates and extended CodeQL default setup for Actions, JavaScript/TypeScript and Python; record every initial alert.
items.outOfScope: Application, database, Render, public-domain behavior, manual alert dismissal or remediation of findings discovered by the initial analysis.
acceptance: Dependabot vulnerability alerts and automated security updates are enabled
Extended CodeQL default setup is configured for Actions, JavaScript/TypeScript and Python with the remote threat model and standard runner
The initial CodeQL analysis succeeds and every Dependabot, code-scanning and secret-scanning alert is read
Every actual CodeQL finding remains open and is assigned to a dedicated remediation issue rather than hidden or dismissed
items.verification: Read the repository security settings, wait for the exact initial CodeQL run, query all three alert APIs and link the retained findings to V039–V041.
items.privacy: Do not upload runtime credentials, private trustee material or personal data; repository analysis must operate only on the public source and established workflow context.
items.fixtures: Exact main commit 7622b76ce88f68e5387d61dbadb75ef5efa92ebb and GitHub-hosted default analysis runners.
items.howToVerify: Follow issue #75 and CodeQL workflow 41212450725; no Browser E2E applies because user-visible behavior is unchanged.

items.title: Remediate unbounded API route operations
items.goal: Bound confirmed expensive API operations against request abuse without changing authorized behavior.
items.scope: Reproduce and remediate CodeQL missing-rate-limiting alerts 1–28 across ballot, identity, management and provider routes.
items.outOfScope: Manual alert dismissal, client-only throttling, unrelated API refactoring, deployment cutover or changes to voting semantics.
acceptance: Every alert 1–28 is mapped to a reproduced route and evidence
Positive and adversarial tests cover the selected request limit and recovery window
A subsequent extended CodeQL analysis closes the remediated alerts without manual dismissal
Existing authorized API behavior and the demand-only public boundary remain intact
items.verification: Reproduce the affected routes under their actual authorization and storage conditions, run focused positive and adversarial tests, and inspect the subsequent CodeQL result.
items.privacy: Do not key request controls on ballot choice, identity attributes or cross-service correlation identifiers.
items.fixtures: Synthetic TEST-PERSON identities, isolated databases and the existing service authorization contracts.
items.howToVerify: Follow issue #76 and code-scanning alerts 1–28; no finding may be dismissed to satisfy the gate.

items.goal: Remove the confirmed time-of-check/time-of-use risk from runtime configuration handling.
items.scope: Reproduce and remediate CodeQL file-system-race alert 36 in scripts/runtime-config.ts.
items.outOfScope: Manual alert dismissal, deployment redesign, unrelated runtime initialization changes or configuration normalization.
acceptance: The current operation and exact race condition are documented from evidence
Positive and adversarial tests cover the corrected file operation
A subsequent extended CodeQL analysis closes alert 36 without manual dismissal
Runtime configuration contracts and deployment behavior remain intact
items.verification: Exercise the exact runtime configuration operation, confirm the causal file-state change, run focused tests and inspect the subsequent CodeQL result.
items.privacy: Never expose generated runtime secrets or private key material in tests, logs, artifacts or issue evidence.
items.fixtures: Synthetic temporary runtime state with no production credentials or trustee material.
items.howToVerify: Follow issue #77 and code-scanning alert 36; no finding may be dismissed to satisfy the gate.

items.title: Audit file-data outbound request boundaries

items.scope: Reproduce and remediate CodeQL file-access-to-http alerts 29–35 in the API and retained in-app Browser coordinator.
items.outOfScope: Manual alert dismissal, replacing the in-app Browser workflow, unrelated networking changes or invented data-flow assumptions.
acceptance: Alerts 29–35 are individually mapped to reproduced inputs, destinations and evidence
Positive and adversarial tests cover the confirmed production boundary
A subsequent extended CodeQL analysis closes remediated alerts without manual dismissal
Test-only classifications remain explicitly separated from production behavior
items.verification: Trace each file input and outbound destination, reproduce the production and test-only paths separately, run focused adversarial tests and inspect the subsequent CodeQL result.
items.privacy: No credential, private key, identity payload, ballot choice or unrestricted local file may cross an outbound request boundary.
items.fixtures: Synthetic public artifacts and explicit temporary test files only; no real identity data or private trustee material.
